prompt:
Role and task instructions:
You, Mia, have been asked to play a hug role in your best friend Hannah's wedding. You are the maid of honor and you are asked to give a speech at the reception.

User request:
You are Mia and is the maid of honor and the best friend of the bride, Hannah. Hannah is marrying Andrew. Your task is to compose an entertaining and heartfelt maid of honor speech for a wedding. This speech should blend humor, personal anecdotes, and genuine emotion to celebrate the couple's special day.
The audience will be a diverse group of wedding guests, including family members of varying ages, friends, and acquaintances of the bride and groom. They are gathered to celebrate and are looking forward to enjoying the festivities. Your speech should cater to this joyful and celebratory mood, being relatable and engaging to all attendees.
Remember, the goal of your speech is to entertain while sincerely honoring the bride and groom. It's an opportunity to add to the joy and celebration of their special day.
answer:
Good evening, everyone! For those I haven’t met yet, I’m Mia, Hannah’s best friend and very proud maid of honor.

Hannah gave me two instructions for tonight: keep it reasonably short, and don’t embarrass her. So I’d like to thank you all for coming. Good night!

Unfortunately for Hannah, I’ve been looking forward to this microphone for years.

Being Hannah’s best friend means having someone who will listen to every detail of your problem, help you solve it, and then check whether you’ve eaten. She’s thoughtful in ways that rarely draw attention. She remembers the appointment you were nervous about. She calls after the difficult conversation. And if you say, “I’m fine,” she somehow knows whether you need space, advice, or fries.

Usually, in my case, fries.

One of my favorite memories is a dinner we decided to cook together. Hannah had chosen an ambitious recipe. I had chosen to believe I could help.

Within an hour, every surface in the kitchen was covered, we’d used approximately fourteen spoons, and the garlic bread had become a small archaeological discovery.

I was ready to declare defeat. Hannah opened a window, put the food we could rescue on our nicest plates, and said, “Come on. We’re still having dinner.”

We ate, we laughed, and I stayed far later than I’d planned. I couldn’t tell you what the main course was supposed to be. I remember being happy.

Andrew, when you came into Hannah’s life, I was paying attention. Best friends do that. It’s a completely unofficial position with absolutely no boundaries.

What won me over were the little things: you asking her a question and really listening to the answer; the way you make her laugh when she’s trying very hard to be serious; how comfortable she is around you.

And Hannah, I noticed you started telling stories with “we” in them. “We found this place.” “We’re thinking about going.” “We tried cooking this.”

That last one concerned me, given our history.

But hearing you build a life together has been such a joy. Andrew, thank you for loving my friend with care, humor, and kindness. I’m so happy she has you, and so happy you have her.

Hannah, we’ve shared so many ordinary days, and they’ve meant more to me than I can say. Getting to stand beside you on this extraordinary one is something I’ll always treasure.

Everyone, please raise a glass.

To Hannah and Andrew: may your home be full of laughter, may you keep finding reasons to celebrate each other, and may you always remember to check the garlic bread.

I love you both. Cheers!
